topic: Perspective: A Technique for Representing Three-Dimensional Depth
passage: In art, there is a number of ways to use perspective to obtain the illusion of width, including using colors and graduated values of black and white, and accurately drawn the subject by applying the rules of the geometric system of perspective.
In order to achieve perspective, you must make a number of observances.
The forms or objects where you draw on a flat surface actually has width and dimension in real life.
As you view them and place their shapes and forms on a drawing surface, try to represent that width to make the objects appearing unrealistic and three-dimensional.
Objects appear different when viewing from various positions.
Because this, it's important to establish the viewpoint, and sticks with it.
When observed a subject, you see width and three dimensions.
When you draw this subject onto a flat surface as it appears to the eye, you are drawn in perspective.
